newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross to send more flour to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross to send more flour to N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's Red Cross will send 700 tonnes of flour to famine-stricken North Korea on Tuesday, the second such shipment in a week, a Red Cross spokesman said Monday.
"We purchased the flour worth 260 million won ($300,000) with donations made by a Catholic organisation and Buddhist organisations," said Rhee Jong-geun.
"We will send the flour tomorrow, and this will be our eleventh shipment."
The South Korean Red Cross stopped shipments of aid to Pyongyang after a North Korean submarine intruded into South Korean waters last September, landing 26 infiltrators.

North Korea apologised in December for the submarine incursion and Seoul returned the remains of 24 North Korean infiltrators shot dead during a manhunt. One was captured alive and the other is still at large.
Resuming aide to the Stalinist North, the South Korean Red Cross shipped 300 tonnes of flour on Friday at the port of Inchon, just west of Seoul.
North Korea, which has been suffering from accute food shortages due to devastating floods in 1995 and 1996, said on Monday it had only half the grain needed to feed its people.
"The nation's annual demand for grain is about 7.84 million tons, of which 4.82 million tons is needed as food," North Korea's official media said.
"Last year's flood damage made the grain output drop to 2,502,000 tons in unhulled state, the amount being far less than expected," the Korean Central News Agency said.

Last week, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said food rations in North Korea had dropped to a level four times lower than normally considered essential for a healthy population
The North Korean agency accused Seoul of "spoiling the atmosphere of international food supply" by underestimating flood damages in the North.
A spokesman of the South Korean Unification Ministry said Seoul would consider offering government-level food aid to North Korea if North Korea made a government-to-government request.
